subtopics.title: Energy, the Joule, and Energy Stored by Position

questions.question: Energy is best described as:
options: The capacity to do work, measured in joules

questions.question: Gravitational potential energy is energy stored because of:
options: The object's position in the gravitational field

questions.question: Read as a lifting bill, m × g × h is:
options: The weight (m × g) times the height lifted — the work done against gravity

questions.question: Potential energy is a scalar, which means:
options: It has magnitude but no direction — joules never point

subtopics.title: Pricing the Lift — 4 Kilograms to 3 Metres

questions.question: The 4 kg tin lifted 3 m gains E p = 4 × 9,8 × 3 =
In the calculation, the intermediate value 39,2 is:
options: The tin's weight in newtons — mass times g

questions.question: The total potential energy on the 10 m platform is:
The FURTHER gain from 3 m to 10 m can be found two ways that agree:
options: 392 − 117,6 = 274,4 J, or weight times the 7 m height difference

subtopics.title: The Reference Level — Where Zero Lives

questions.question: Measured from a cellar 2 m below ground, the tin on the 3 m platform has E p =
options: 196 J — because h becomes 5 m from that zero

questions.question: The ground observer says 117,6 J; the cellar observer says 196 J. Who is right?
options: The ground observer, because the ground is the true zero
The cellar observer, because lower is more accurate
Neither — the tin has no energy until it falls
Both — each value is correct relative to its own declared zero

questions.question: Both bookkeepers agree on the energy released in a fall to the ground because:
options: Nature only cashes in energy differences, and the zero-point disagreement subtracts away
They round to the same number
The cellar observer converts to ground units

questions.question: The forbidden move with reference levels is:
options: Choosing the lowest point as zero
Declaring the level in the first line
Mixing two different levels inside one problem
Letting an object sit below the zero

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: A question supplies a WEIGHT of 39,2 N. The m in E p = mgh must be:
options: 4 kg — the weight divided by g
Zero until the mass is stated

questions.question: A wheelbarrow is pushed 8 m up a ramp that rises 2 m. The h in mgh is:
options: 2 m — only the vertical height counts

questions.question: Which answer commits the scalar trap?
options: '117,6 J downward' — energy never carries a direction

questions.question: This topic leads next to:
options: Kinetic energy and the conservation of mechanical energy

subtopics.title: The Bank Account in the Sky

questions.question: In the water-tower picture, pumping water up overnight is:
options: A deposit — work banked as potential energy

questions.question: The two halves of the lifting bill m × g × h are:
options: Mass times height, then times two
The weight (m × g) and the height it is lifted through

questions.question: One joule is roughly:
options: The energy of a moving truck
The output of a power station in an hour
The effort of lifting a small apple through one metre
The heat of a boiling kettle

questions.question: The account pays out its stored energy when:
options: The object falls — height converts back to speed

questions.question: The 4 kg tin's weight is:
The deposit for the 3 m hoist is:
The top-up from 3 m to 10 m costs 274,4 J by both roads because:
options: Both roads round to the same value
The platforms are the same height
Gravity charges per metre climbed — only the change in height matters
The weight doubles on the higher platform

questions.question: Hard hats matter on site because a falling tin:
options: Loses its energy on the way down
Converts every stored joule — all 392 from 10 m — back into speed

questions.question: Two observers give the same platform different potential energies because:
options: They measure heights from different chosen zeros

questions.question: Physics escapes the two-zeros paradox because:
options: The ground is legally the zero
Nature only ever pays out energy differences, which agree from any zero
The two observers average their answers

questions.question: The recommended choice of reference level is:
options: The highest point, so all energies are negative
The lowest point in the problem, declared in the first line

questions.question: An object below your chosen zero has:
options: The same energy as at zero
Negative potential energy — an overdrawn but meaningful balance
